exposure: fertility-sparing treatment for early-stage endometrioid endometrial cancer (EEC) or endometrial atypical hyperplasia (EAH)
reproductive methods (in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET), ovulation induction, natural conception)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 481 patients with early-stage endometrioid endometrial cancer or endometrial atypical hyperplasia who desired to conceive after successful fertility-sparing treatment from January 2015 to June 2023.
finding: Assisted reproductive technologies like IVF-ET and ovulation induction resulted in higher pregnancy and live birth rates compared to natural conception in patients with EEC/EAH after fertility-sparing treatment, though IVF-ET was associated with a higher incidence risk of threatened abortion, preterm birth, and placenta accreta/increta.
